chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafth from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave while he had a debt, fleeing from the debt. He said: 'There is no emancipation for him, and if he emancipated him while in good health and soundness, there is no claim for the creditor against him.'

key_terms.تَدْبِير: Emancipation of a slave upon the owner's death
key_terms.فِرَاراً مِنَ الدَّيْن: Fleeing from the debt (to avoid creditors)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's emancipation if the owner did it to avoid paying debts?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the validity of 'tadbir' (emancipation upon death) when an owner incurs debt specifically to evade creditors, ruling that such emancipation is invalid to prevent fraud. Conversely, if the owner was in sound health and the debt was not incurred solely for this purpose, the creditor cannot claim the emancipated slave, protecting the slave's status. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle of examining the owner's intent (niyyah) and the nature of the debt to ensure justice in inheritance and manumission.
